title: Dynamic instrumentation bootstrapper and header normalization for cross-service tracing
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem:
Currently our tracing coverage across SDKs and HTTP middleware is fragmented: various services send different header formats (B3, W3C traceparent, vendor headers), some SDKs register hooks eagerly and add measurable latency, and legacy clients drop sampling decisions. This makes trace stitching, sampling determinism, and observability dashboards unreliable.

Goals:
- Provide a lightweight, dynamic instrumentation bootstrapper that lets SDKs and frameworks register tracing hooks at runtime with a single canonical registration API.
- Normalize inbound trace headers to a canonical carrier so downstream services see a single trace format (primary: W3C traceparent), while preserving original headers for backward compatibility when needed.
- Implement deterministic sampling override rules and a safe fallback when no sampling decision is present.
- Offer middleware adapters for common frameworks (Express, Fastify, Django, FastAPI) that are opt-in and add minimal overhead.

Non-goals:
- We will not replace full OpenTelemetry SDKs in every runtime during this ticket. This work is an interoperability shim and bootstrapper to make existing and future SDKs behave consistently.

Technical approach (high level):
1) Hook registry: a tiny runtime API (registerHook, unregisterHook, listHooks) exposed by our internal SDK packages. Hooks are executed in a deterministic order: context-extract -> sampling -> span-start -> span-decorators -> span-end handlers. Hooks must be async-safe and return quickly.
2) Header normalization: inbound headers accepted: "traceparent" (W3C), "b3" / "x-b3-*", and our legacy "x-rw-trace". The middleware canonicalizes these into a single internal carrier header "x-rw-canonical-trace" (opaque value derived from the W3C traceparent) and attaches an immutable header "x-rw-original-trace-formats" listing normalized sources. If a request contains multiple conflicting sampling decisions, we apply deterministic resolution rules (see below).
3) Sampling rules: default deterministic sampler uses a hashed stable key (user_id > request_id > ip) and a global sampling rate token. We support header-driven overrides for debugging ("x-rw-trace-force=1") that require RBAC/whitelisting.
4) Compatibility shim: SDKs that still rely on B3 will read the canonical carrier and keep their internal span IDs; outgoing requests will include both W3C and legacy headers for a transition window.
5) Performance guardrails: the bootstrapper keeps per-request overhead minimal by caching parsed header values in request-local storage and avoiding allocations in hot paths. We will add a fast-path that skips normalization for known-internal-clients via a feature flag.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Using OpenTelemetry as the only abstraction versus a small internal shim: we chose a shim to avoid forcing major dependency upgrades in every service and to provide a low-overhead fast-path. We will provide an OTEL adapter that maps the shim to OTEL spans for services that adopt OTEL.
- Canonicalizing to W3C traceparent increases compatibility with external partners but requires careful handling of sampling bits from legacy B3 headers. The normalization step therefore preserves original headers in a metadata header for debugging.

Rollout and compatibility strategy:
- Implement feature-flagged middleware and SDK bootstrapper (feature: dynamic_trace_hooks).
- Canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100%.
- During canary we will enable a compatibility mode where both canonical and original headers are emitted on outbound calls. After 8 weeks of monitoring, flip to single-format outbound.

Monitoring and acceptance criteria (see acceptance_criteria field):
- End-to-end trace coverage (trace completeness) >= 99% for instrumented services after rollout.
- No more than 1% p50 latency regression on the bootstrapper path vs baseline.
- Dashboards for trace sampling distribution, header normalization errors, and hook execution latency live in Console.

comments: 2026-02-18 Maya Chen: created ticket after spike — PoC shows header normalization works across local services, recorded small allocation spikes in Node SDK.
2026-02-21 Luca Romano: initial implementation of registerHook/unregisterHook landed in internal SDK, see PR #4120. Still working on async-shim for FastAPI.
2026-02-24 Design review: PM and Platform reviewed header canonicalization. Request to add 'x-rw-original-trace-formats' header for debugging and to limit size to 256 bytes.
2026-02-26 QA: Integration tests show 0.8% p50 regression on Node when hooks are enabled; Java shows negligible impact. Prepare perf micro-optimizations.

acceptance_criteria: Implement registerHook API and provide SDK adapters for Node and Python (Express + FastAPI).
Middleware canonicalizes inbound headers to x-rw-canonical-trace and sets x-rw-original-trace-formats when needed.
Deterministic sampling implementation with override header gated by RBAC.
Unit tests and integration tests added to the tracing integration harness; end-to-end tests included in CI.
Performance: p50 latency regression <= 1% on bootstrapped path under 500 RPS load in staging.
Observe trace completeness and header-normalization error rate on canary dashboard; error rate < 0.1% to progress rollout.
rollout_plan: Gate feature behind dynamic_trace_hooks FF (false by default).
Canary 5% of traffic for two days; monitor header-normalization errors and trace completeness.
If stable, increase to 25% for one week and create a follow-up to evaluate removing legacy outbound headers.
25% -> 60% -> 100% with dashboards and rollback playbook documented.
After 8 weeks of stable telemetry, flip global outbound to single-format (W3C) and remove legacy header emission in runtime-1.23.
Post-rollout: run a compatibility sweep and notify partners of header changes via integration channel.
